title: Hard Guarantees over Hope: Deterministic Control for LLM Agents
description:
This work separates stochastic perception from deterministic control in LLM agents. The model proposes content; code types, admits, and decides. Decisions whose invariance is promised do not depend on uncanonicalized stochastic model output.

We distinguish trajectory disagreement from output disagreement and show that, under a deterministic non-model stack, eliminating delegated branching makes the trajectory independent of model randomness and localizes output discrepancies to shared nodes. The executable architecture implements propose → type → verify/admit → decide with typed provenance, policy-as-code, feasibility filters, assurance floors, abstention, and offline policy adaptation without weight updates. Its guarantee is same belief base ⇒ same decision, not same prompt ⇒ same response.

The mechanism is evaluated on a controlled synthetic benchmark of 78 forensic-document tasks, 12 agent paradigms, and 3 replicates, without an LLM judge. Between 12% and 28% of cells show different utilities at temperature zero, but the current setup does not separate delegated branching from serving-stack nondeterminism. An in-sample intervention replaces one model-selected anchor with code and moves one paradigm from 0.33 to 0.89 while raising pass^3 from 0.33 to 0.67; transfer remains preregistered. Capability-based generalization is suggestive rather than established (eight arms, exact p=0.066). A learned cost policy saves 41% against a constant policy with a confidence interval crossing zero, so it is reported as partial evidence, not as a validated selector.

Scope. Structural results are stated for agents in general under their assumptions. Empirical magnitudes apply only to this benchmark, panel, and models. Provenance records how a value was obtained; it does not certify truth.
notes: Written in Spanish. Formal identities and finite operational instances have executable checks. Empirical claims are reported with their scope, denominator, uncertainty, and relevant noise floor.
